daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo has ordered the acceleration of Prambanan temple restoration from an estimated 200 years to just three years, with Culture Minister Fadli Zon explaining the project will create jobs for tradespeople and vocational school graduates. The restoration may use new stones if originals are unavailable, Fadli added. Separately, Prabowo attended the 79th National Cooperatives Day peak event and met with Luhut to discuss economic conditions and GovTech.

  • The MPR and Supreme Court signed an agreement on judicial independence, with MPR Chair stating the Supreme Court lacks 1,600 judges and urging law graduates to become judges with salaries of Rp 50 million per month.
  • National Police Chief responded to Mahfud MD regarding the transfer of the case against former Deputy Attorney General for Special Crimes Febrie Adriansyah, after the police chief visited the TNI Commander and Attorney General amid controversy over the case.
  • The Ministry of Immigration confirmed that former Deputy Attorney General Febrie has been banned from travel for 20 days, while civil society groups urged the public to monitor the case to prevent it from fading.
  • A DPR member expressed concern about a potential national strike by MBG kitchen partners after an association threatened to lock kitchens, following their complaints to the DPR about suspensions after poisoning incidents.
  • The Home Affairs Minister warned village heads to carefully manage village funds, noting that mismanagement carries criminal penalties, while separately calling on local governments to strengthen supply and distribution to control inflation.
  • A DPR member proposed national standards for Islamic boarding schools following an incident in which a student was burned in Lombok.
  • The Attorney General's Office is auctioning 90 apartment units belonging to Benny Tjokro with a limit value of Rp 219.7 billion, while prosecutors also alleged corruption funds from a railway project flowed to Gus Miftah.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia expressed confidence in Iran's commitment to peaceful resolution of the Strait of Hormuz crisis, with MPR Speaker revealing that Iran has invited President Prabowo to visit Tehran. Indonesia also urged the US and Iran to respect the Islamabad Memorandum amid escalating tensions in the region.

  • NU Chairman Gus Yahya called for Middle East peace after attending the funeral of Ayatollah Khamenei in Iran, while Gerindra Secretary-General Ahmad Muzani called for an end to war at the same funeral.
  • A Deputy Foreign Minister clarified that security agreements with Indonesia are not like AUKUS, distinguishing Indonesia's approach from the trilateral security pact.
  • Indonesia's Minister for the Protection of Migrant Workers said UN CMW Committee recommendations strengthen protection for Indonesian migrant workers abroad.
  • Indonesia stated it will use trade to build peace amid global fragmentation, emphasizing economic diplomacy as a tool for international cooperation.

Other

The Communications and Digital Ministry announced it has blocked 3.7 million online gambling sites since October 2024, with the minister stating the crackdown must target the entire ecosystem. Authorities uncovered a modus operandi involving farmers and housewives paid Rp 100,000-500,000 to open bank accounts for gambling operators.

  • Jakarta Governor Pramono visited the LRT Jakarta Phase 1B project site, with the line set to operate in August 2026 and the provincial government planning to review LRT tariffs.
  • President Prabowo inaugurated two dams in Aceh capable of irrigating 26,889 hectares of agricultural land, while Agriculture Minister Amran distributed Rp 1 billion for mosque repairs in Bener Meriah.
  • Danantara named partners for phase 2 of waste-to-energy projects, while the environment agency warned that waste facilities will collapse by 2028 without proper management.
  • Indonesia stepped up chemical regulations to advance its OECD membership bid, while the national bullion bank has accumulated 153 tons of gold according to the ministry.
  • Indonesia secured $30 million in Japanese investment for the plasma industry and a new Indonesia-Russia partnership in the palm oil sector backed by BPDP.
